title: Why Are Property Bridging Loans Popular in the UK?
summary: Blog article (not a case study). Only a fragment of the page surfaced in search results; the full argument was not visible. According to the search tool's summary of the visible portion, the article's thesis is that bridging loans are a long-established UK finance option used by both first-time buyers and experienced investors, and that they are popular because bridging lenders apply more flexible underwriting than mortgage providers, which shortens approval to a few weeks. The concrete guidance revealed is a trade-off: bridging loans carry higher interest rates than mortgages, so they suit short-term rather than long-term use. No eligibility criteria, process steps, FAQ, pricing, lender names, calls to action or author/date were revealed for this specific page.
